entry.title: The golden rule of gold! Amirhossein Khaleqi, a political economy researcher,…
entry.summary:
Source: @RahbordChannel

The golden rule of gold! Amirhossein Khaleqi, a political economy researcher, says in the program "Economy Politics" that to predict the trend of gold, before any analysis, one must answer a question: Is trust increasing or decreasing? According to him, whenever people's trust in the financial system, government, and economy weakens, the tendency toward assets that preserve their value in the long term increases, and gold is the most important safe haven for capital in such conditions. Khaleqi explains that humans are inevitably dependent on trust to preserve the value of their assets; either on human institutions like fiat money and governments, or on nature and limited assets like gold, whose supply has grown at a relatively constant rate throughout history. From his perspective, when governments damage this trust through inflation or monetary policies, capital moves back toward gold. To watch the full program, click here. What will happen? Signing a memorandum of understanding (if it is signed) was a signal to the Yankees to moderate the initial image of war based on the irrational behavior of the Iranian side and take the deal more seriously. It was also a powerful maneuver for Mr. Qalibaf, showing that he has the necessary influence to advance his will; after all, he is someone with whom one can deal! But such consolidation of power in a "country of parallel powers" is difficult. Assuming his dominance over the domestic scene, how much flexibility will the "strong man" have? Is giving up uranium reserves (at least 400-some kilograms) and nuclear restrictions acceptable to Iran, and can this be sold to the established powers? The answer to this question will indicate how seriously the probability of an agreement (with any content) can be taken. But perhaps the more likely scenario is that these very parties are more prepared for a more devastating war than the previous ones; the Arabs will face a difficult challenge in neighboring the Islamic Republic after an agreement, and a sudden leap from "cutting off the snake's head" to good neighborliness is not very likely; Israel is also unlikely to miss this opportunity to pursue its interests; on the American domestic scene, merely opening the Strait of Hormuz is not considered a serious achievement and is far from "unconditional surrender." On demagoguery: Demagogic politicians around the world use certain principles whose examples are not hard to find: 1. Questioning the speaker's motives: When someone presents a solid and documented argument, the demagogue does not say "this argument is wrong." Instead, he says: "Why is this person saying this? Creating cynicism toward everything: The demagogue goes a step further and says: everyone lies, the media are corrupt, experts care about their own interests, politicians are all the same. entry.title: If the Arabs do not price oil in dollars, should we say goodbye to dollar…
entry.summary:
Source: @RahbordChannel

If the Arabs do not price oil in dollars, should we say goodbye to dollar hegemony? You have probably heard a lot that the dollar's superior position in the world has one clear reason: America's historical collusion with the oil-rich Arab states of the Persian Gulf to price oil in dollars (especially after the oil shock of the seventies and even before that). So if the Arabs give up pricing in dollars and, for example, turn to the yuan, dollar hegemony will also go away! But in an interesting Financial Times article, it is said that this is not the case. The percentage of countries' dollar foreign exchange reserves alone does not tell us much. Basically, the current position of the dollar depends more on a more important factor than the power of the Yankee government: the Eurodollar system! But what does Eurodollar mean? It means dollars outside the borders of America! Dollars over which the Federal Reserve (the central bank) does not have serious control. In fact, about 40% of the world's dollars, i.e., about 14 trillion dollars, are not inside America, and banks around the world (London, Tokyo, or even Dubai) themselves create dollars in their accounting books and lend to customers and settle; for final settlement, of course, America comes into play, but this system should be considered more "non-governmental" and "decentralized." The irony of history is that the initial motivation for creating the Eurodollar system was brought about by the Soviet government. Also, precedent and habit are part of the story; the dollar is the common language of the business community. Merchants around the world prefer to denominate their contracts in dollars for convenience and risk management. This is what is also called the network effect, meaning when others act in a certain way, you also follow the rest for your own convenience. Moreover, Yankee treasury bonds are considered the safest assets in the world, and there are trillions of dollars of debt worldwide that must be repaid in dollars, so demand for this currency always exists; even if oil sales in dollars stop. To summarize, contrary to popular belief, dollar hegemony will not collapse with a change in the unit of oil pricing (e.g., China's yuan). The dollar is the operating system of the world's private banking and has an extensive network that is very difficult, if not impossible, to replace. Although we are always doomed to be surprised by the future, God knows best. https://bit.ly/4tBrjlX Rahbord Channel/Amirhossein Khaleqi @RahbordChannel Support Rahbord: https://bit.ly/2Hja5HY

entry.title: The story of Shir Del, oil, and the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has threatened that…
entry.summary:
Source: @RahbordChannel

The story of Shir Del, oil, and the Strait of Hormuz. Trump has threatened that if the Iranians do not accept his conditions—namely, a complete halt to enrichment, missile restrictions, and not supporting his proxy groups in the region—he will resort to military options. Iran's situation is also not good for various reasons, and in response to the Yankees' threat, it has said that the card of closing the Strait of Hormuz is on the table, and of course, the oil facilities of neighboring countries will not be safe either. In a report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies, four oil scenarios have been outlined, and reviewing them is worthwhile: The first scenario is America preventing Iran's production and seizing its exports; Kharg Island and oil tankers are the main targets, and the consequence is cutting 1.6 million barrels of daily exports to China; in this relatively low-risk scenario for the Yankees, we will see a $10-12 increase in crude oil prices. The second scenario is Iran disrupting shipping in the Persian Gulf, carried out with speedboats, drones, anti-ship missiles, and mining in the Strait of Hormuz; here, about 18 million barrels of Arab countries' oil exports are at risk. We will witness oil prices jumping above $90, which will also push gasoline prices in America above $3. The UAE and Saudi Arabia can use alternative routes to the Strait of Hormuz to a very limited extent, but Iraq, Kuwait, and Qatar have no way to export their oil except through the Strait of Hormuz. The third scenario is an American attack on Iran's oil facilities, aimed at destroying the loading docks of Kharg Island, oil platforms, and oil infrastructure, and oil prices will likely rise above $100 because Iranian oil will be out of the market for a long time. The fourth scenario is a direct Iranian attack on the oil facilities of neighboring Arab countries, targeting oil fields, refineries, and export terminals of Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, and other countries, and similar to the time of Russia's attack on Ukraine, it might even push oil prices above $130. As a personal opinion, scenarios two and four can create deterrence as a threat, but if implemented, they would have serious consequences on the scale of regime change for the Islamic Republic, and given the current situation, I doubt they are on Tehran's agenda right now. May God protect Iran, but we must wait and see what the future holds; God knows best. https://bit.ly/4rrK0Y1 Channel Rahbord/Amirhossein Khaleghi @RahbordChannel Support Rahbord: https://bit.ly/2Hja5HY
